questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the word CANON (not CANNON)?
options: A) The literary canon includes Shakespeare works.
B) The soldiers fired the canon at the enemy fort.
C) The canon ball flew over the city walls.
D) Load the canon with gunpowder.
explanation: CANON (one N) means a general law or principle; a list of accepted works. CANNON (two Ns) is a large gun. The literary CANON is a list of accepted great literary works.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses ELICIT (not ILLICIT)?
options: A) The question was designed to elicit a specific response.
B) He was caught in an elicit gambling ring.
C) The elicit drug trade was investigated by police.
D) The smugglers dealt in elicit goods.
explanation: ELICIT means to draw out a response or reaction. ILLICIT means forbidden by law or rules. The question was designed to ELICIT (draw out) a response is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses AURAL (not ORAL)?
options: A) Her aural comprehension improved after music lessons.
B) The aural examination required writing essays.
C) She delivered an aural presentation to the committee.
D) The aural test checked her writing skills.
explanation: AURAL means relating to the ear or hearing. ORAL means relating to the mouth or spoken language. AURAL COMPREHENSION involves understanding what you hear.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses DISCRETE (not DISCREET)?
options: A) The research divided participants into four discrete groups.
B) She was asked to be discrete about the confidential information.
C) He handled the sensitive matter in a discrete manner.
D) Please be discrete when discussing private affairs.
explanation: DISCRETE means individually separate and distinct. DISCREET means careful and circumspect in speech; not attracting attention. Four DISCRETE (separate) groups is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses COMPLEMENT (not COMPLIMENT)?
options: A) The wine was a perfect complement to the meal.
B) He received many complements for his speech.
C) She paid her a lovely complement.
D) The dress received complement from all the guests.
explanation: COMPLEMENT means something that completes or goes well with something else. COMPLIMENT means a polite expression of praise. The wine COMPLEMENTED (completed) the meal.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses FLAIR (not FLARE)?
options: A) She has a natural flair for languages.
B) The rescue team sent up a flair to signal their location.
C) The solar flair disrupted communications.
D) She decorated the room with lots of flair-up details.
explanation: FLAIR means natural talent or stylish elegance. FLARE means a sudden burst of light or flame. She has a natural FLAIR (talent) for languages is correct.

questionText: Which sentence uses PRINCIPAL correctly (not PRINCIPLE)?
options: A) The principal reason for the delay was bad weather.
B) She stood by her principals throughout the crisis.
C) His principals were unshakeable.
D) The principals of honesty guided his decisions.
explanation: PRINCIPAL means first in importance (adjective) or the head of a school (noun). PRINCIPLE means a rule or moral belief. The PRINCIPAL (main) reason is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses VENAL (not VENIAL)?
options: A) The venal official accepted bribes in exchange for contracts.
B) The priest assured him that lying was a venal sin.
C) She committed a venal sin by arriving late to church.
D) The church distinguished between venal and mortal sins.
explanation: VENAL means susceptible to bribery; corrupt. VENIAL means a sin that is minor and pardonable. A VENAL official is one who accepts bribes; a VENIAL sin is a minor one.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses AFFECT (verb, not EFFECT)?
options: A) The cold weather affected the harvest.
B) The medicine had a positive affect.
C) The new law will affect in major changes.
D) His injury had no affect on his performance.
explanation: AFFECT is usually a verb meaning to have an impact on. EFFECT is usually a noun meaning a result or consequence. The weather AFFECTED (impacted) the harvest is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses EMINENT (not IMMINENT or IMMANENT)?
options: A) She is an eminent scholar in the field of neuroscience.
B) The storm is eminent; we must take shelter immediately.
C) The philosopher argued that God is eminent in all creation.
D) Disaster seems eminent given the current situation.
explanation: EMINENT means famous and respected; prominent. IMMINENT means about to happen. IMMANENT means inherent; present throughout. An EMINENT scholar is a highly respected one.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses TORTUOUS (not TORTUROUS)?
options: A) The tortuous mountain path wound back and forth for miles.
B) The experience was tortuous, causing intense suffering.
C) The examination was tortuous to the point of being cruel.
D) He found the tortuous interrogation extremely painful.
explanation: TORTUOUS means full of twists and turns; excessively lengthy and complex. TORTUROUS means involving or causing torture or great suffering. A winding mountain path is TORTUOUS.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses FLOUNDER (not FOUNDER)?
options: A) Without clear leadership, the project began to flounder.
B) The ship began to flounder and eventually sank.
C) His business foundered for several months before improving.
D) She foundered on stage, forgetting her lines.
explanation: FLOUNDER means to struggle to move or act; to be confused. FOUNDER means to fail completely; or (of a ship) to sink. The project began to FLOUNDER (struggle) is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses LOATH (not LOATHE)?
options: A) He was loath to admit that he had made a mistake.
B) She loath public speaking and avoided it whenever possible.
C) I loath the taste of overcooked vegetables.
D) He loath his new commute to work.
explanation: LOATH (adjective) means reluctant or unwilling. LOATHE (verb) means to feel intense dislike. He was LOATH (reluctant) to admit his mistake is correct usage of the adjective.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses WREAK (not WRECK)?
options: A) The storm wreaked havoc on the coastal town.
B) The teenagers wrecked havoc in the shopping centre.
C) The disease wrought havoc across the population.
D) Both A and C are correct
explanation: WREAK HAVOC and WROUGHT HAVOC are both correct. WREAK means to cause damage or harm; its past tense is wreaked or (archaic) wrought. WRECK means to destroy an object; you cannot wreck havoc.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses PORE (not POUR)?
options: A) She spent hours poring over the ancient manuscripts.
B) He poured over the documents looking for errors.
C) She poured over every detail of the contract.
D) He poured his energy into poring the wine.
explanation: PORE (verb) means to study something carefully and attentively. POUR means to cause liquid to flow. She PORED OVER (studied carefully) the manuscripts is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses GRISLY (not GRIZZLY)?
options: A) The crime scene was described as a grisly discovery.
B) The hikers spotted a grisly bear on the trail.
C) The grisly bear is the largest North American land carnivore.
D) He was a large, grisly-haired man.
explanation: GRISLY means causing horror or disgust; gruesome. GRIZZLY refers to the grizzly bear or means streaked with grey. A GRISLY discovery is a horrifying one.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses REIN (not REIGN or RAIN)?
options: A) She kept a tight rein on the department budget.
B) The king reined for forty years.
C) She reigned in her spending after the budget cuts.
D) The horses were released from their reigns.
explanation: REIN refers to a strap used to control a horse; figuratively, to restrain or control. REIGN means to rule as king or queen. RAIN is precipitation. A TIGHT REIN on spending means careful control.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses HALE (not HAIL)?
options: A) Despite his age, he was still hale and hearty.
B) She was haled as the greatest poet of her generation.
C) The crowd haled the returning hero with cheers.
D) He was hale before the court to answer charges.
explanation: HALE (adjective) means strong and healthy. HAIL means to greet enthusiastically, or frozen precipitation. HALE AND HEARTY describes someone robust and in good health.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses ASSAY (not ESSAY)?
options: A) The geologist sent the rock sample for chemical assay.
B) He wrote a brilliant assay on Victorian literature.
C) The teacher assigned an assay on climate change.
D) Her assay explored themes of identity and belonging.
explanation: ASSAY means a test or analysis, especially of metal ore content; to test or evaluate. ESSAY means a piece of writing on a subject. A rock sample for CHEMICAL ASSAY is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses GAMUT (not GAUNTLET)?
options: A) The performance ran the gamut from comedy to tragedy.
B) The new employee had to run the gamut of tests.
C) She threw down the gauntlet, challenging him to a debate.
D) Both A and C are correct
explanation: GAMUT means the complete range of something. GAUNTLET is a glove or a form of punishment (run the gauntlet). Both options A and C use the correct words correctly.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses PORTEND (not PRETEND)?
options: A) The dark clouds seemed to portend a storm.
B) He portended to be asleep when his mother entered.
C) She portended illness to avoid the meeting.
D) The child portended to fly by flapping his arms.
explanation: PORTEND means to be a sign or warning of (an imminent event, typically an unwelcome one). PRETEND means to act as if something is true when it is not. Dark clouds PORTEND a storm.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses CACHE (not CASH)?
options: A) Archaeologists discovered a cache of ancient coins.
B) She paid with cache rather than a credit card.
C) The shop only accepts cache payments.
D) He kept a large cache of money in the bank.
explanation: CACHE means a hidden or reserved store of something. CASH means money in coins and notes. A CACHE of ancient coins is a hidden hoard of them.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses MARTIAL (not MARITAL)?
options: A) The country was placed under martial law after the uprising.
B) They sought marital advice from the relationship counsellor.
C) Both A and B use the correct words
D) The general showed great marital discipline.
explanation: MARTIAL means related to war or fighting. MARITAL means relating to marriage. Both option A (MARTIAL law) and option B (MARITAL advice about marriage) use the correct words.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses CALLOUS (not CALLUS)?
options: A) His callous disregard for others shocked everyone.
B) The guitar player had callous on his fingertips.
C) She developed a callous from years of manual work.
D) The callous on his heel caused him to limp.
explanation: CALLOUS (adjective) means showing no empathy; hardened emotionally. CALLUS (noun) means an area of hardened skin. His CALLOUS disregard uses the adjective correctly.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses DIFFUSE (not DEFUSE)?
options: A) The light was diffused through the frosted glass panel.
B) She tried to diffuse the bomb before it exploded.
C) The expert was called to diffuse the explosive device.
D) He diffused the situation by making people laugh.
explanation: DIFFUSE means to spread over a wide area; to make less concentrated. DEFUSE means to remove the fuse from a bomb; to reduce tension. Light DIFFUSED through frosted glass is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses RETICENT (not RELUCTANT)?
options: A) She was reticent about sharing personal details in public.
B) He was reticent to lend his car to his brother.
C) The child was reticent to eat the vegetables.
D) She was reticent to take the job offer.
explanation: RETICENT means not revealing one thoughts or feelings; reserved in speech. RELUCTANT means unwilling. Being RETICENT ABOUT SHARING PERSONAL DETAILS captures the meaning of being verbally reserved.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses ENVY (not JEALOUSY)?
options: A) She felt envy when she saw her colleague new office.
B) He experienced jealousy when he saw a colleague with something he wanted.
C) Both A and B describe the same emotion correctly.
D) Envy is felt about someone you do not know.
explanation: ENVY is wanting something someone else has. JEALOUSY involves fear of losing something you already have (usually a relationship) to someone else. Wanting a colleague new office is ENVY, not jealousy.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses APPRAISE (not APPRISE)?
options: A) The estate agent was called to appraise the property value.
B) Please appraise me of any new developments immediately.
C) She was appraised of the situation before the meeting.
D) He appraised his colleague of the client complaint.
explanation: APPRAISE means to assess or evaluate the value of something. APPRISE means to inform someone of a fact. The estate agent APPRAISED (evaluated) the property value.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses INFER (not IMPLY)?
options: A) From the evidence, we can infer that she left early.
B) What are you trying to infer by that comment?
C) His tone inferred that he was unhappy with the result.
D) The report inferred that profits would fall.
explanation: INFER means to conclude from evidence; a reader or listener infers. IMPLY means to suggest without stating directly; a writer or speaker implies. We (readers) INFER from evidence.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses MITIGATE (not MILITATE)?
options: A) Extra training helped mitigate the risks of the operation.
B) His poor record mitigated against him getting the promotion.
C) The new policy militated the financial losses.
D) Her apology mitigated against any further damage.
explanation: MITIGATE means to reduce the severity of something. MILITATE (against) means to be a factor that works against something. Training MITIGATED (reduced) the risks is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses PROGENY (not PRODIGY)?
options: A) The king was concerned about which of his progeny would inherit.
B) The young progeny could play complex music at age four.
C) Mozart was described as a musical progeny.
D) The science progeny won a national award at age twelve.
explanation: PROGENY means offspring or descendants. PRODIGY means a young person with exceptional abilities. The king PROGENY are his children and descendants.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses ENDEMIC (not EPIDEMIC or PANDEMIC)?
options: A) Malaria is endemic in many tropical regions.
B) The disease was endemic, spreading rapidly across several continents.
C) The endemic spread of flu affected millions worldwide.
D) The endemic outbreak required international emergency aid.
explanation: ENDEMIC means regularly found among particular people or in a certain area. EPIDEMIC means a widespread disease in a region. PANDEMIC means worldwide spread. Malaria is ENDEMIC (regularly present) in tropical regions.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses CREDULOUS (not CREDIBLE)?
options: A) The credulous child believed everything the magician told him.
B) The credulous witness gave a compelling account in court.
C) Her credulous testimony was backed by solid evidence.
D) The credulous report was accepted as reliable by all experts.
explanation: CREDULOUS means too ready to believe; gullible. CREDIBLE means believable and convincing. A CREDULOUS child is one who believes things too easily.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses COMPLACENT (not COMPLAISANT)?
options: A) Success made him complacent, and his performance declined.
B) The complacent host made every effort to please his guests.
C) She was complacent in accommodating all the requests.
D) The complacent assistant was eager to help with any task.
explanation: COMPLACENT means smugly self-satisfied; uncritically pleased with oneself. COMPLAISANT means willing to please; agreeable. Success made him COMPLACENT (self-satisfied and careless) is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses VERACIOUS (not VORACIOUS)?
options: A) She was known as a veracious journalist who never distorted facts.
B) The veracious reader finished three books every week.
C) He was a veracious eater who never wasted food.
D) The shark is a veracious predator in ocean ecosystems.
explanation: VERACIOUS means truthful and accurate. VORACIOUS means wanting or devouring large quantities; very eager. A VERACIOUS journalist is one committed to the truth.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses PRESCRIBE (not PROSCRIBE)?
options: A) The doctor prescribed antibiotics for the infection.
B) The new regulations prescribe gambling in public areas.
C) The law prescribed the use of certain chemicals.
D) The judge proscribed her to community service.
explanation: PRESCRIBE means to authorise a medicine or to recommend. PROSCRIBE means to forbid or prohibit. The doctor PRESCRIBED (authorised) the antibiotics is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses SANGUINE (not SANGUINARY)?
options: A) Despite setbacks, she remained sanguine about the project outcome.
B) The battle was sanguine, resulting in thousands of casualties.
C) The sanguine conflict left the region devastated.
D) The sanguine war lasted three years with heavy bloodshed.
explanation: SANGUINE means optimistic and positive. SANGUINARY means involving much bloodshed. Despite setbacks, she remained SANGUINE (optimistic) is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses TURBID (not TURGID)?
options: A) The turbid river water was too murky to see through.
B) The turbid prose of the legal document bored all readers.
C) His turbid writing style was full of pompous language.
D) The politician gave a turbid and inflated speech.
explanation: TURBID means (of liquid) cloudy or opaque; muddy. TURGID means (of language) excessively pompous and complex. The TURBID (murky) river water is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses LUXURIANT (not LUXURIOUS)?
options: A) The tropical island had luxuriant vegetation covering every surface.
B) The luxuriant hotel suite had silk sheets and marble floors.
C) They spent the weekend in a luxuriant spa resort.
D) She treated herself to a luxuriant five-star experience.
explanation: LUXURIANT means rich and profuse in growth; abundant. LUXURIOUS means highly comfortable and expensive. The LUXURIANT (abundant, lush) vegetation of a tropical island is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses OBLIVIOUS (not OBVIOUS)?
options: A) He was oblivious to the danger and walked straight into the trap.
B) It was oblivious that she had not prepared for the interview.
C) The oblivious answer was clearly written in the first paragraph.
D) The solution was oblivious to anyone who read the instructions.
explanation: OBLIVIOUS means not aware of or not concerned about what is happening around one. OBVIOUS means easily perceived or understood. He was OBLIVIOUS TO (unaware of) the danger is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses MARTIAL (not MARITAL) in a different context?
options: A) She holds a black belt and has studied martial arts for fifteen years.
B) They were having martial difficulties and sought counselling.
C) The marital artist defeated all challengers.
D) Their marital conflict was resolved through mediation.
explanation: MARTIAL ARTS refers to disciplines such as karate, judo, and kung fu. MARITAL relates to marriage. She studied MARTIAL ARTS (fighting disciplines) is correct.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses AMBIVALENT (not AMBIGUOUS)?
options: A) She was ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
B) His ambivalent statement could mean two completely different things.
C) The ambivalent results of the experiment confused the scientists.
D) Her ambivalent response left everyone uncertain about her position.
explanation: AMBIVALENT means having mixed feelings about something; uncertain. AMBIGUOUS means open to more than one interpretation. She was AMBIVALENT ABOUT (had mixed feelings about) accepting the job.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses ELUDE (not ALLUDE)?
options: A) The meaning of the poem eluded most readers.
B) In his speech, he eluded to the recent scandal.
C) She eluded to the problem without naming it directly.
D) He eluded to the fact that changes were coming.
explanation: ELUDE means to escape from or avoid; to be difficult to understand or remember. ALLUDE means to make indirect reference to. The poem ELUDED (escaped the understanding of) most readers.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses CORROBORATE (not COLLABORATE)?
options: A) Two witnesses corroborated the defendant story.
B) The scientists corroborated on the research project together.
C) She corroborated with her team to complete the report.
D) The artists corroborated to create the mural.
explanation: CORROBORATE means to confirm or support a statement or theory. COLLABORATE means to work jointly with others. Two witnesses CORROBORATED (confirmed) the story.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses FEIGN (not FAIN)?
options: A) She feigned illness to avoid the examination.
B) He would fain have gone, but he had no choice.
C) She feigned happiness at the news of his success.
D) Both A and C are correct
explanation: FEIGN means to pretend; to simulate. FAIN is an archaic word meaning willing or eager. Both SHE FEIGNED ILLNESS and SHE FEIGNED HAPPINESS correctly use feign to mean to pretend.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses JEJUNE (not JUVENILE)?
options: A) The critic dismissed the novel as jejune and unsophisticated.
B) The court handled the case in the jejune justice system.
C) She attended a special school for jejune offenders.
D) The programme addressed the needs of jejune delinquents.
explanation: JEJUNE means naive, simplistic, and unsophisticated; (of ideas) lacking interest or significance. JUVENILE means relating to young people. The novel JEJUNE means it is intellectually superficial.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses PERSPICACIOUS (not PERSPICUOUS)?
options: A) The perspicacious detective immediately identified the key clue.
B) Her perspicacious explanation made the theory easy for all to follow.
C) The perspicacious writing style made the complex topic accessible.
D) The teacher praised the perspicacious clarity of the essay.
explanation: PERSPICACIOUS means having a ready insight; shrewdly perceptive. PERSPICUOUS means clearly expressed and easy to understand. The PERSPICACIOUS (perceptive) detective identified the clue.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses PRESCIENT (not PRESENT)?
options: A) She was prescient in predicting the economic downturn years before it happened.
B) All team members were prescient at the morning meeting.
C) The prescient award was given to the most improved player.
D) He was prescient at the ceremony and accepted the award.
explanation: PRESCIENT means having or showing the ability to know what will happen in the future; prophetically accurate. PRESENT means being in a place or existing now. She was PRESCIENT (prophetically accurate) in predicting the downturn.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses NOXIOUS (not OBNOXIOUS)?
options: A) The factory was releasing noxious fumes into the atmosphere.
B) His noxious behaviour made him unpopular at every party.
C) She found his noxious personality difficult to tolerate.
D) The noxious guest dominated every conversation.
explanation: NOXIOUS means harmful or poisonous; very unpleasant. OBNOXIOUS means extremely unpleasant in behaviour or character. NOXIOUS FUMES are harmful chemical gases; OBNOXIOUS behaviour is deeply unpleasant.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses TORPID (not TORRID)?
options: A) The warm afternoon left him feeling torpid and unable to concentrate.
B) The novel was a torpid love affair set in the Arizona desert.
C) Their torpid romance was passionate and intense.
D) The torpid summer was filled with dramatic events.
explanation: TORPID means mentally or physically inactive; lethargic. TORRID means very hot and dry; passionate. Feeling TORPID (sluggish and inactive) on a warm afternoon is correct usage.
